subject: Mathematics
topic: Sets and two- or three-set Venn diagrams
scope: IGCSE Core/Extended: set language and two-set Venn diagrams. Extended: three-set diagrams, membership, empty-set and subset notation. No GCSE Number coverage is claimed for this lesson. Original teaching and practice, not official exam questions. Tier labels describe intended specification scope, not predicted grades. Author-proposed coverage is recorded separately from independent review and publication approval.
objectives: Translate between set descriptions, lists and notation.
Construct and interpret two-set Venn regions without double counting.
Use Extended notation and three-set regions where required.

notes.heading: IGCSE both tiers: universal set, complement and set definitions
paragraphs: A set is a collection of distinct elements. Order in a written list is irrelevant and repetitions do not create new elements. The universal set U states the allowed universe. With U={1,2,3,4,5,6}, define A={2,4,6}, the even members. Its complement A′={1,3,5} contains elements of U not in A. Changing U can change A′, so always identify the universe.

n(A) is the number of elements, here 3. A set-builder description gives a rule: B={x: x is an integer and 1≤x<4} means B={1,2,3}. The endpoints matter: the inequality excludes 4. A finite list and a rule can describe the same set, but the rule must include the intended number type; all real numbers between 1 and 4 would be an infinite set instead.

notes.heading: IGCSE both tiers: two-set construction and counting
paragraphs: A∩B is the intersection: elements in both. A∪B is the union: elements in at least one, including those in both. Draw a rectangle for U and two overlapping circles A and B. The four disjoint regions are A only, A∩B, B only and outside both. Place each element in exactly one region. To shade A∩B shade just the lens; to shade A∪B shade both complete circles; to shade (A∪B)′ shade the rectangle outside both circles.

When totals are given, fill the overlap first. With 20 students, 12 in A, 9 in B and 5 in both, the A-only region has 12−5=7 and the B-only region 9−5=4. The union contains 7+5+4=16, leaving 4 outside. Equivalently n(A∪B)=n(A)+n(B)−n(A∩B); subtraction removes the overlap counted twice. Core Venn diagrams are limited to two sets.

notes.heading: IGCSE Extended: membership and subsets
paragraphs: The notation x∈A means x is an element of A; x∉A means it is not. The empty set ∅ contains no elements. If every element of A belongs to B, then A is a subset of B, written A⊆B here; A⊈B means at least one element of A is outside B. Some specifications and questions use ⊂ for subset: follow the convention stated in the question, especially if strict containment is relevant. Membership compares an element with a set, while subset compares two sets.

For U={1,2,3,4}, A={2,4} and B={1,2,3,4}, we have 2∈A and A⊆B, but {2} is a subset rather than the number 2 itself. If two sets have no shared elements their intersection is ∅; that does not make either set empty. Since the empty set has no counterexample element, it is a subset of every set.

notes.heading: IGCSE Extended: three-set regions
paragraphs: Three overlapping circles split the universe into eight disjoint regions: A only, B only, C only, A-and-B only, A-and-C only, B-and-C only, all three and outside all. Put the triple intersection in first. If n(A∩B)=8 and the triple intersection contains 3, then A-and-B only contains 5, because the pairwise intersection includes the triple region unless the question says only.

After the three pair-only regions, use each set total to obtain its single-only region. Add all seven internal regions once to find the union, then subtract from the universe for the outside region. The formula n(A∪B∪C)=n(A)+n(B)+n(C)−n(A∩B)−n(A∩C)−n(B∩C)+n(A∩B∩C) follows the same count correction. Re-add the regions within each original circle as a check. Negative region counts indicate inconsistent data or double subtraction.

workedExamples.prompt: Let U={1,…,10}, A be multiples of 2 and B be multiples of 3. Describe all four Venn regions.
steps: List A={2,4,6,8,10} and B={3,6,9}. Place the common element 6 first.
Remove 6 from each list for the single-only regions, then find unused members of U.
workedExamples.answer: A only={2,4,8,10}; overlap={6}; B only={3,9}; outside={1,5,7}.

workedExamples.prompt: [Extended] In a group of 40, n(A)=20, n(B)=18, n(C)=15, n(A∩B)=8, n(A∩C)=7, n(B∩C)=6 and n(A∩B∩C)=3. Find all regions.
steps: Subtract the triple 3 from each pair total to get 5,4,3.
Subtract each circle’s pair-only and triple counts from its total, obtaining 8,7,5.
The seven inside regions sum to 35; subtract from 40.
workedExamples.answer: Triple=3; AB only=5; AC only=4; BC only=3; A only=8; B only=7; C only=5; outside=5.

misconceptions.correction: Union means at least one set and includes the overlap.

misconceptions.claim: A pairwise intersection in a three-set question means exactly two sets.
misconceptions.correction: It includes the triple intersection unless the word only or an equivalent exclusion is stated.

flashcards.back: The number of elements in A.

flashcards.front: What is A′ relative to U?
flashcards.back: All elements of U that are not in A.
The elements common to both sets.
The elements in at least one of the sets.

flashcards.front: Where should a three-set count diagram start?
flashcards.back: In the triple intersection, then pair-only regions.

questions.prompt: [IGCSE Core/Extended] Let U={1,2,…,12} and A={x: x is an integer, 3≤x<8}. List A, A′ and n(A).
solution: Include the lower boundary 3 and exclude 8.
Take the complement only within the stated U.
markingPoints: List A and its count correctly.

questions.prompt: [IGCSE Core/Extended] Draw two overlapping circles inside U={1,…,8}. Put A={1,2,4,8} and B={2,3,5,8} into the four regions. List A∩B and A∪B.
questions.answer: A only={1,4}; overlap={2,8}; B only={3,5}; outside={6,7}. Intersection={2,8}; union={1,2,3,4,5,8}.
solution: Place 2 and 8 in the overlap first.
Place every remaining member once, then read intersection and union from the regions.
markingPoints: Place all elements in correct disjoint regions.

questions.prompt: [IGCSE Core/Extended] On a two-circle Venn diagram describe precisely which region to shade for A∩B′ and for (A∪B)′.
questions.answer: A∩B′ is A only; (A∪B)′ is outside both circles but inside U.
solution: A∩B′ requires being in A and not in B.
The complement of the union excludes every point in either circle.
markingPoints: Identify the outside-both region within U.

questions.prompt: [IGCSE Core/Extended] Among 35 learners, 19 study French, 16 study German and 7 study both. Find the counts for French only, German only and neither.
solution: Subtract the overlap from each set total.
markingPoints: Give the neither count without double counting.

questions.prompt: [IGCSE Extended] For U={1,2,3,4,5}, A={2,4} and B={2,3,4}, decide whether 2∈A, 5∈B, A⊆B and B⊆A are true. Find A∩{1,3,5}.
questions.answer: True, false, true, false; the intersection is ∅.
solution: 2 is an element of A; 5 is not an element of B.
Every A element is in B, but 3 in B is not in A; no A element is odd.
markingPoints: Assess the membership and subset statements correctly.
Give the empty intersection and explain the counterexample to B⊆A.

questions.prompt: [IGCSE Extended] Draw three-set Venn regions for a group of 50 with totals A=24, B=22, C=20; pairwise intersections AB=10, AC=9, BC=8; triple=4. Find exactly one set, exactly two sets and none.
questions.answer: Exactly one=24; exactly two=15; none=7. Regions: A only=9, B only=8, C only=7, AB only=6, AC only=5, BC only=4, triple=4.
solution: Deduct these from set totals to find singles 9,8,7; all internal regions total 43.
markingPoints: Calculate all pair-only and single-only regions.
Sum exactly-one and exactly-two counts separately.

questions.prompt: [IGCSE Extended] Describe the regions shaded by (A∩B)∩C′ and by (A∪B∪C)′ in a three-set Venn diagram.
questions.answer: The AB-only lens excluding C; the outside-all region within U.
solution: The first expression requires A and B membership but excludes every C member.
The second excludes the entire union of the three circles.
markingPoints: Exclude the triple region from the first shading.
Identify the complement of the three-set union.

revisionGuide.summary: Venn regions are disjoint pieces, while set totals overlap. State the universe, fill intersections first and re-add every original total. Core uses two sets; Extended also uses three sets and additional notation.
keyIdeas: What does n(A) represent? The number of elements in A.
What is A′ relative to U? All elements of U that are not in A.
What is A∩B? The elements common to both sets.
What is A∪B? The elements in at least one of the sets.
Where should a three-set count diagram start? In the triple intersection, then pair-only regions.
